metadata.repo_type_justification: Application source code (pricing.cpp) with a deployable entry point (main()), a Dockerfile, and Kubernetes deployment manifests present.
metadata.archetype_justification: No database connections or writes detected; the single CGI endpoint performs read-only pricing lookup from a static flat file with no user-specific state.

findings.title: Managed Compute — containerized for EKS but no cluster IaC
findings.description: The application is containerized with a multi-stage Dockerfile and has Kubernetes deployment manifests targeting EKS with 2 replicas, resource limits, and health probes. However, no IaC defines the EKS cluster itself.
findings.gap: No IaC defines the EKS cluster — the Kubernetes manifests assume the cluster exists. The Dockerfile uses httpd:2.4-alpine with mod_cgi rather than a purpose-built container runtime.
findings.recommendation: Define the EKS cluster infrastructure in Terraform/CDK. Consider replacing the Apache CGI model with a lightweight HTTP server built into the binary.

findings.title: Network Security — no network policies defined
findings.description: The Kubernetes Service is ClusterIP (internal-only) with hardened security context, but no NetworkPolicy resources exist to enforce pod-to-pod segmentation.
findings.gap: No Kubernetes NetworkPolicy to restrict ingress/egress. No explicit network segmentation beyond ClusterIP service type.
findings.recommendation: Add a Kubernetes NetworkPolicy to restrict ingress to only the expected upstream services/ingress controller. Deploy an Ingress resource with the AWS ALB Ingress Controller.

findings.title: API Entry Point — no gateway or load balancer configured
findings.description: No API Gateway, ALB, or CloudFront configured as entry point. The service is ClusterIP-only with no active Ingress resource.
findings.gap: No managed entry point with throttling, authentication, or request validation.
findings.recommendation: Deploy the commented ALB Ingress resource or define an API Gateway entry point with throttling and request validation.

findings.title: Auto-Scaling — static replica count with no HPA
findings.description: The Kubernetes Deployment has a static replicas: 2 with no HorizontalPodAutoscaler configured.
findings.gap: Static capacity provisioning — cannot scale up during traffic spikes or scale down during low demand.
findings.recommendation: Add a Kubernetes HPA targeting CPU or request-rate metrics with appropriate min/max bounds.

findings.title: High Availability — no multi-AZ topology constraints
findings.description: The Deployment specifies 2 replicas but no topology spread constraints or pod anti-affinity rules. Both pods could be scheduled in the same AZ.
findings.gap: No AZ fault isolation configured. A single AZ failure could take down both replicas.
findings.recommendation: Add topologySpreadConstraints with topologyKey: topology.kubernetes.io/zone to ensure replicas are distributed across AZs.

findings.title: Infrastructure as Code — no IaC exists
findings.description: No Terraform, CloudFormation, CDK, or Pulumi files present. The service depends on EKS, VPC, ECR, and IAM — none defined in-repo.
findings.gap: 0% IaC coverage for the infrastructure this service depends on.
findings.recommendation: Define supporting infrastructure (EKS cluster, VPC, ECR, IAM) in Terraform or CDK.

findings.title: CI/CD Automation — no pipeline exists
findings.description: No CI/CD pipeline exists. The original deployment was manual scp. No GitHub Actions, GitLab CI, Jenkins, or CodeBuild configuration found.
findings.gap: All deployments are manual. No automated build, test, or deploy stages.
findings.recommendation: Create a CI/CD pipeline that builds the Docker image, pushes to ECR, runs tests, and deploys to EKS.

findings.title: Programming Languages — pre-C++11 with CGI execution model
findings.description: C++ (pre-C++11) using only C standard library. CGI execution model (process-per-request). Known buffer overflow and XSS vulnerabilities.
findings.gap: Legacy language version with no cloud-native tooling. CGI model has significant performance overhead. No AWS SDK integration possible without rewrite.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite in a modern cloud-native language (Go, Python, Node.js). The service is ~70 lines of logic, making a rewrite low-effort.

findings.title: Monolith vs Microservices — single file with no modular structure
findings.description: Single deployable unit — a single C++ source file with no module boundaries, no interfaces, and no separation of concerns.
findings.gap: No modular structure — parsing, data access, and presentation intermixed in a single file.
findings.recommendation: In a rewrite, separate concerns into distinct modules (input parsing, data access, response formatting) following hexagonal architecture.

findings.title: API Versioning — no versioning strategy
findings.description: No API versioning exists. The single endpoint /cgi-bin/pricing.cgi has no version prefix or headers.
findings.gap: No versioning strategy — any API contract change breaks all consumers simultaneously.
findings.recommendation: Adopt URL-path versioning (e.g., /api/v1/pricing) in a rewrite.

findings.title: Service Discovery — Kubernetes DNS-based discovery
findings.description: Kubernetes Service provides DNS-based discovery within the cluster with standard labels applied.
findings.gap: No service mesh for advanced traffic management. Discovery is basic Kubernetes DNS only.
findings.recommendation: Current Kubernetes DNS-based discovery is adequate. Integrate into service mesh if platform adopts one.

findings.title: Unstructured Data Storage — pricing data locked in local flat file
findings.description: Pricing rules stored in a flat pipe-delimited file baked into the Docker image. Updates require container rebuild or volume remount.
findings.gap: Data locked in local filesystem. No managed object storage, no accessibility for other systems.
findings.recommendation: Migrate pricing rules to Amazon S3 with caching, or DynamoDB for low-latency key-value lookups.

findings.title: Unified Data Access Layer — centralized but lacking abstraction
findings.description: Data access centralized in a single lookup_price() function. Single point of data access, though it lacks abstraction (raw C file I/O).
findings.gap: No data access abstraction — raw fopen/fgets/sscanf with hardcoded data format.
findings.recommendation: In a rewrite, define a PricingRepository interface that abstracts the data source from business logic.

findings.title: API Authentication — no authentication on endpoint
findings.description: No authentication of any kind on the CGI endpoint. Any entity with network access can query pricing data.
findings.gap: Completely unauthenticated API — no OAuth2, JWT, API key, or any auth mechanism.
findings.recommendation: Add authentication at the API Gateway/Ingress layer (ALB with Cognito, or API Gateway with Lambda authorizer).

findings.title: Centralized Identity — no identity provider integration
findings.description: No identity provider integration. No Cognito, OIDC, SAML, or federated identity.
findings.gap: No centralized identity integration — cannot participate in SSO or federated access policies.
findings.recommendation: Integrate with a centralized IdP (Cognito, Okta) at the ingress/gateway layer.

findings.title: Compute Hardening — partial hardening, no patching strategy
findings.description: Container hardening partially implemented (non-root user, dropped capabilities). No vulnerability scanning or patching automation.
findings.gap: No vulnerability scanning, no automated patching, no base image update process. Base images will drift from security patches.
findings.recommendation: Configure ECR image scanning. Add Dependabot/Renovate for base image updates. Consider distroless images.

findings.title: Application Security Pipeline — no security scanning
findings.description: No security scanning tools configured. Known vulnerabilities (buffer overflow, XSS) go undetected.
findings.gap: Zero security validation in any pipeline. No SAST, DAST, dependency scanning, or container scanning.
findings.recommendation: Integrate SAST (Semgrep, CodeGuru) and container scanning into the CI/CD pipeline.

findings.title: Distributed Tracing — no tracing instrumented
findings.description: No OpenTelemetry, X-Ray, or any tracing SDK in the application or deployment configuration.
findings.gap: No request tracing — impossible to trace requests through the system.
findings.recommendation: Add X-Ray daemon as a sidecar. In a rewrite, instrument with OpenTelemetry SDK.

findings.title: SLO Definitions — no SLOs defined
findings.description: No SLO definitions, CloudWatch alarms, or monitoring configured in-repo.
findings.gap: No formal SLOs — no availability target, no latency percentile targets, no error budget.
findings.recommendation: Define SLOs for the pricing endpoint (p99 latency < 100ms, availability > 99.9%).

findings.title: Business Metrics — no custom metrics published
findings.description: No custom business metrics. The CGI binary writes only the HTTP response to stdout — no logging or metrics.
findings.gap: No visibility into business-level behavior — no pricing lookup counts, no SKU-not-found rates.
findings.recommendation: In a rewrite, publish custom metrics: pricing lookups per SKU, cache hit rates, SKU-not-found rates.

findings.title: Anomaly Detection — no alerting configured
findings.description: No CloudWatch alarms, no anomaly detection, no PagerDuty/OpsGenie integration.
findings.gap: No proactive alerting — operators learn of issues only through external observation.
findings.recommendation: Add CloudWatch Container Insights. Create alarms on error rates, pod restarts, and response latency.

findings.title: Deployment Strategy — rolling update only
findings.description: Default Kubernetes RollingUpdate with readiness probes. No canary, blue/green, or traffic shifting.
findings.gap: No staged rollout — a bad deployment affects 50% of traffic immediately with 2 replicas.
findings.recommendation: Implement canary deployments using Argo Rollouts or Flagger with progressive traffic shifting.

findings.title: Integration Testing — no automated tests exist
findings.description: No automated tests of any kind — no unit tests, integration tests, contract tests, or end-to-end tests.
findings.gap: No regression safety net. Any code change has no automated way to verify correctness.
findings.recommendation: Add smoke tests (curl-based endpoint validation), parsing tests, and integration tests in CI pipeline.

findings.title: Incident Response — no runbooks or automation
findings.description: No incident response automation. No runbooks, no SSM documents, no self-healing beyond pod restarts.
findings.gap: Incident response is entirely ad hoc. No documented procedures for common failure modes.
findings.recommendation: Create runbooks for common incidents (rules.dat corruption, high error rates, OOM kills).

findings.title: Observability Ownership — no ownership defined
findings.description: No CODEOWNERS, no team-attributed dashboards, no named alarm owners.
findings.gap: No defined ownership of monitoring and observability for this service.
findings.recommendation: Add a CODEOWNERS file. Tag dashboards and alarms with the owning team.
